why: Both moved identical traffic with the same two-client hook and both verified it live, so the decision rests on system-level judgment — and only A does the thing the brief asks for: it attacks calls rather than just configuring them (deleting the one-tool inner financials agent, skipping sourceless query engines, and proposing collapsing the two-level agent that costs two serial round trips before any token reaches the user), while also covering labels, per-role models, tier, timeout, fallbacks, model_map, Shadow models and Switchyard, with measured per-shape prices. B is a careful, well-measured migration tune-up — three config branches, no question anywhere about whether a call should exist, nothing at rework scale, and its one cheap unbuilt idea is an http connection pool.
A_best: It found the places where the model is doing no work: the per-document financials agent whose only tool takes no arguments and always returns the same payload (2 Router calls → 1, measured), the question engine offered with no sources, and the top-level agent whose entire decision is 'qualitative or quantitative' — plus a per-conversation prompt_cache_key measured at −39%/−65% on the one call that carries the whole history.
B_best: The strongest evidence in either report on the model question: full SubQuestionQueryEngine turn latency per candidate (gpt-4o-mini 5.5s vs gpt-6-luna 17.5s standard / 24.1s Flex), a three-arm live fall-through test proving the fallback actually serves this app's tool schema, and the d2 insight that the Router key's spend cap is now a single point of failure for the product's only feature — correctly tied to reading the runtime's fallback condition.
A_worst: Branch hygiene and statistics: three improvement branches are cut from llm-roles so their diffs are entangled (disclosed, but a reviewer must apply them in order), four branches carry a validation flag that OPENAI_API_KEY references were removed even though embeddings and the provider-fallback path still need it, and the headline model/latency numbers are n=1 per arm with the rework's latency gain computed by arithmetic rather than measured.
B_worst: It never questions whether any of the five-to-twenty calls per turn should exist, offers nothing above config scale, and its prompt_cache_key is a single constant per label ('sec-insights.chat') shared across all conversations rather than per conversation — a weaker key than the per-conversation one A measured; its claim that deepseek-v4-flash is the only temperature- and tool-capable non-OpenAI catalog model is also contradicted by A's live-verified gpt-oss-120b surviving the capability guard.
